QF.id: SIA Social Impact Assessment and Assessors_26

question.text: For a Social Impact Assessment, baseline measurement is critical because:

answer.text: It establishes the starting point in the project/programme, allowing later mid-line and end-line assessments to measure what changed due to the intervention
It replaces the need for any further data collection during the engagement
It is only relevant for financial audits, not SIA
It is used exclusively for CSR rule 8(3) assessments and not for SSE-listed SEs

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 5.11.4 'Need Assessments / Obtaining Program Understanding' states: 'The baseline measurement is needed to establish the starting point in any project/programme/project-based activity. Later mid-line and end-line assessments give the auditor insight on the opportunities and challenges for the social audit. Establishing the baseline is critical to measure what changed due to the intervention.' The Trap: B overstates — baseline is foundational but additional data collection is always required. C is wrong — baseline is SIA-specific terminology. D is wrong — baseline applies broadly including SSE-listed engagements. Cross-Exam Context: Baseline analysis appears in NISM XV (RA) as 'base period' for time-series and in XXIII as 'baseline' for impact measurement — different disciplines but same logical role. Assessor's Pro-Tip: If the SE didn't conduct a baseline, reconstruct it retrospectively using secondary data (census, NFHS, ASER, village records) — document limitations clearly in the AIR's 'Overall Approach & Methodology' section.
